# Appearance: Colours and Layers {#sec-appearance}

::: {.chapter-abstract}
Eight records to make a pin orange.
Why the colour is attached to the geometry from the outside, how a colour reaches a single face, and where the layers went.
:::

The clamp assembly was exported with the bracket grey and the pins orange.
Both colours are in the file, and neither is anywhere near the geometry it colours.
Here is the pin's:

```step
#318 = MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION('',(#319),#302);
#319 = STYLED_ITEM('color',(#320),#249);
#320 = PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT((#321));
#321 = SURFACE_STYLE_USAGE(.BOTH.,#322);
#322 = SURFACE_SIDE_STYLE('',(#323));
#323 = SURFACE_STYLE_FILL_AREA(#324);
#324 = FILL_AREA_STYLE('',(#325));
#325 = FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOUR('',#326);
#326 = COLOUR_RGB('',0.800000010877,0.500000003429,0.199999998682);
```

Nine records, of which one carries the colour and one names the thing being coloured.
The rest is Part 46 — *visual presentation* — doing what the integrated resources always do: expressing a simple idea in terms general enough to cover every kind of presentation anyone might want.

## Reading the chain {#sec-appearance-reading-the-chain}

From the bottom:

- `#326` `COLOUR_RGB` — red 0.8, green 0.5, blue 0.2. Components are reals from 0 to 1. The name is empty. (The values are not quite 0.8, 0.5 and 0.2 because they passed through single-precision floats on the way; this is normal.)
- `#325` `FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOUR` — a colour used for filling areas. The alternative is a hatch pattern or a tile.
- `#324` `FILL_AREA_STYLE` — a set of fill styles (here, one). Fill styles are what a *face* gets; curve styles are what an *edge* gets.
- `#323` `SURFACE_STYLE_FILL_AREA` — the fill style applied as a surface style element. Other elements exist for boundaries, silhouettes, parameter lines, rendering.
- `#322` `SURFACE_SIDE_STYLE` — a set of surface style elements for one side of a surface.
- `#321` `SURFACE_STYLE_USAGE` — that side style applied to `.BOTH.` sides of the surface (or `.POSITIVE.` or `.NEGATIVE.`).
- `#320` `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` — a set of styles (here, one surface style usage) to be assigned together.
- `#319` `STYLED_ITEM` — the assignment. `name` is `'color'`, `styles` is `(#320)`, and `item` is `#249`: the pin's `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`. This is the record that connects appearance to geometry, and it does so by pointing *at* the solid — the solid does not know it has a colour.
- `#318` `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` — a representation whose items are styled items, in the same geometric context as the geometry it decorates (`#302`). Its job is to be a container that the AP can require and a reader can look for: *find every representation of this type, and you have found every colour in the file.*

Every colour in every AP214 or AP242 file follows this chain.
The middle five records are almost always exactly these, differing only in instance numbers, and once you have read one you can skim the rest.
What varies is the two ends: which colour, and which item.

## What gets coloured {#sec-appearance-what-gets-coloured}

`STYLED_ITEM.item` can point at any representation item.
In practice:

**A solid.** As here.
The whole body takes the colour.
This is what most exporters write for a part with a single body colour, and it is what a viewer applies by default to every face of the solid.

**A face.** `STYLED_ITEM('',(#s),#88)` with `#88` an `ADVANCED_FACE` colours one face.
Files with per-face colours have one styled item per face, and they can number in the thousands.
When a face colour and a body colour both apply, the face wins; AP214 formalises this with `OVER_RIDING_STYLED_ITEM`, a subtype of `STYLED_ITEM` with an extra attribute pointing at the styled item it overrides, but many exporters simply write both and rely on the reader to prefer the more specific one.

**An edge or a curve.** Via a `CURVE_STYLE` instead of a surface style: `CURVE_STYLE('',#font,POSITIVE_LENGTH_MEASURE(0.1),#colour)` — a line font, a width (a wrapped measure, as @sec-schema predicted), a colour.
Edge colours appear in wireframe exports and in PMI annotation geometry.

**A mapped item or a whole representation**, so that an assembly component can be coloured as a unit without touching the child's geometry.
Less common.

The pin's colour is on the pin's *solid*, `#249`, which belongs to the pin's product.
Both occurrences of the pin are therefore orange, because both are instances of the same product and there is one solid.
Had the CAD system coloured pin-2 differently, the exporter would have had to either duplicate the pin's geometry as a second product or style a `MAPPED_ITEM`; different systems make different choices, and "instance colour" is one of the features most often lost in exchange.

## Named colours {#sec-appearance-named-colours}

`COLOUR_RGB` is one of two colour entities.
The other:

```step
#340 = DRAUGHTING_PRE_DEFINED_COLOUR('red');
```

A `DRAUGHTING_PRE_DEFINED_COLOUR` has only a name, from a fixed list: `'red'`, `'green'`, `'blue'`, `'yellow'`, `'magenta'`, `'cyan'`, `'black'`, `'white'`.
It stands in for the RGB triple wherever one is expected.
It is inherited from the drawing-exchange parts of the standard, where line colours were symbolic, and is what a few exporters write for their default palette.
A reader must map the eight names to values itself.

## Layers {#sec-appearance-layers}

CAD systems group entities onto named layers, and Part 46 carries them:

```step
#350 = PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('Fasteners','pins and bolts',(#249,#41));
```

A name, a description, and a set of the representation items on the layer.
As always, the layer points at its members; a face does not know its layer.
A file's layers are found by collecting every `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` and inverting.
Layer assignments are far less common in STEP than in native CAD files: many exporters do not write them, and when they do the members are typically solids rather than faces.
AP203 first edition has no layer entity at all.

## Visibility {#sec-appearance-visibility}

A layer can be switched off, or an item hidden, with `INVISIBILITY`:

```step
#360 = INVISIBILITY((#319));
```

— a set of styled items (or layer assignments, or presentation representations) that are not to be displayed.
Its context is a `PRESENTATION_STYLE_BY_CONTEXT` or a draughting model, and it is rare in mechanical exchange except inside saved views, which belong to @sec-pmi.

## Names on geometry {#sec-appearance-names-on-geometry}

Not appearance, but often asked about in the same breath: *where is the name of a face?*
Every representation item has a `name` attribute, and it is almost always `''`.
Some systems — NX and Creo among them, when asked — write the user's face or body name there: `ADVANCED_FACE('Mounting surface',(#18),#52,.F.)`.
Nothing else in the standard carries "the name of face 7," and a system that does not put it in the name slot has no way to send it.
The same is true of feature names, which do not survive export at all: a STEP file knows nothing about holes, fillets or pockets, only about faces.

::: {.callout-warning title="In the wild: What AP203 files cannot say"}
`STYLED_ITEM`, `COLOUR_RGB` and `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` are not in AP203 first edition (`CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN`).
A file with that schema is grey and layerless by definition.
Files exist that declare `CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN` and contain colour records anyway; strict readers drop the colours, lenient ones keep them, and the CAx Implementor Forum's recommended practice is to write AP214 or AP242 if colours matter.
AP203 second edition added presentation; AP242 carries everything here.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="In brief"}
Colour reaches geometry from the outside: a `STYLED_ITEM` points at a solid, face or curve and at a `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT`, which descends through five fixed records to a `COLOUR_RGB` or a named colour.
Styled items are collected in a `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION`.
Face colours override body colours.
Layers are `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT`s listing their members.
Face names live in `representation_item.name`, when they live anywhere.
:::
